Q1: The British hold it. A Union Jack flies from the tower on the Rock in frames 40-41 (Jan 1780). The Rock is not shown with any other flag.
Q2: '1779 — The Great Siege' (frame 23, 21 Jun 1779). Rows of tents and a long line of troops and animals build up on the plain facing the Rock, and ships gather in the bay, so it is a siege of the town by an army and fleet.
Q3: The pictures do not show hunger directly. They suggest the town is cut off. A besieging camp blocks it on land, and ships sit offshore. A few ships come and go in the bay, but the pictures show no food, no starving people and no rations, so my answer is partly inference. Not sure.
Q4: Ships. A single ship and later a small group of ships sail across the bay toward the town (frames 36-38, 47 and 52). The pictures do not show what they carry or that they relieve the town. Not sure what the ships bring.
